As of 2026, YES!Delft has supported more than 600 startups, 82% of which are still active or have been acquired, collectively raising over €1 billion in funding. What happens to startups after they finish a YES!Delft program? After completing the Accelerator, a startup becomes a YES!Delft alumni and keeps access to mentors, experts, investors, and partners for at least 5 years. This long-term support is reflected in the outcomes: of the 560+ startups YES!Delft has supported, 83% are still active or have been acquired. YES!Delft is widely regarded as one of the leading deeptech incubators & accelerators in Europe. What is the difference between the Validation Program, the Accelerator, and the Deep-dive tracks? The Validation Program helps early-stage founders test their business idea and reach first customers. The Accelerator supports startups that already have a validated idea and helps them scale, without taking equity. DecipHER received Pre-Seed investment from Graduate Ventures | YES!Delft YES!Delft Search Menu Latest DecipHER received Pre-Seed investment from Graduate Ventures Published June 22nd, 2026 DecipHER women secures investment to advance AI-driven early detection and prevention of peripartum and postpartum depression. Women’s health startup DecipHER women has secured new pre-seed investment from Graduate Ventures to accelerate the development of its AI-driven platform for the early detection and prevention of peripartum and postpartum depression. The investment marks an important milestone in the company’s mission to transform maternal mental healthcare through earlier intervention and more personalised care. Peripartum and postpartum depression affects an estimated 10–20% of mothers worldwide, yet care pathways remain largely reactive, with intervention often occurring only after symptoms become severe. With approximately 130 million births globally each year, the need for earlier, more precise detection has become increasingly urgent. DecipHER is addressing this challenge by developing a diagnostic platform designed to identify women at risk before symptoms escalate into crisis. By enabling healthcare providers to intervene earlier, the company aims to improve outcomes for mothers while reducing long-term healthcare burdens. Radiopharmaceuticals are an emerging cancer treatment with high potential, but their widespread adoption is hindered by quality control.
